# Table structure goldens

Two kinds of golden live here.

## Synthetic fixtures (`synthetic/`, committed with their PDFs)

Each file reproduces one failure mode a real filing demonstrated: two schemas
stacked in one band, two tables separated by prose, an exhibit index with
wrapped description cells, a ruled grid, a table introduced by a sentence whose
short last line sits directly above its header, and four negatives — a bullet
list, a numbered list, a chart and a two-column prose layout. The PDFs are
generated by

```powershell
py scripts/make_table_fixtures.py
```

which derives each golden from the layout it drew, not from detector output, so
the fixtures stay an independent oracle. `tests/test_table_benchmark.py` runs
them, and they need no local corpus, so they gate CI.

## Corpus goldens (`<pdf-stem>.page-<n>.json`)

These reference PDFs in `test-imports.local/`, which are not committed. Generate
candidates with:

```powershell
py scripts/score_tables.py "test-imports.local/financial-statements/apple 10k.pdf" `
  --write-candidates output/table-candidates
```

Visually inspect each candidate against the rendered page — `scripts/render_table_overlay.py`
draws them, and `--show-rejected` shows what was discarded and why — before
copying approved `<pdf-stem>.page-<n>.json` files here. The scorer intentionally
does not bless detector output automatically, because doing so would make the
detector its own oracle.

A golden containing `"tables": []` is a **negative**: the page must produce no
suggestion at all. Chart pages, bullet lists and numbered lists are recorded that
way, and they are the cheapest goldens to write, because they need no inspection
of boundaries — only the judgement that the page holds no table.

## What the scorer measures

`scripts/score_tables.py` matches predictions to goldens by area overlap rather
than array position, so a missed first table no longer shifts every later
comparison. It reports table-level precision/recall/F1, row and column boundary
precision/recall at a configurable tolerance, header row-count accuracy,
over-merge and over-split counts, and runtime per document and page, and can
write the whole thing as JSON with `--write-report` for comparing two
implementations.

The scanned fixtures rely on direct single-block OCR for pages whose source text
geometry is empty or extremely sparse; that path needs the bundled Tesseract, so
those documents only score in an environment where the worker runtime is
installed. Header labels in those goldens are visually transcribed when OCR does
not recover the body text.
